memory_update.text: For AI data-center power/cooling balance-of-plant, keep VRT and ETN as reference anchors, but do not let them crowd out direct second-order suppliers like POWL and MOD.
POWL maps to medium-voltage switchgear and packaged electrical systems; MOD maps to data-center cooling, hybrid cooling, and liquid-cooling thermal management.
Next Layer 1B pass should search below $10B for pumps, valves, heat exchangers, transformers, busway, coolant distribution units, commissioning, electrical installation, and MEP labor bottlenecks.
Several once-underfollowed AI infrastructure beneficiaries have re-rated above $10B by June 2026; market-cap screen alone may miss still-obscure but no-longer-small suppliers.
POWL should remain in the Layer 1B universe as a medium-voltage switchgear and packaged electrical systems candidate with explicit 2026 AI/data-center backlog commentary.
AAON should remain in the Layer 1B universe as a data-center thermal-management candidate; BASX disclosures provide unusually direct evidence for air-side and liquid-cooling demand.
ATKR is a speculative-shadow candidate for electrical balance-of-plant exposure; keep only if later evidence quantifies data-center revenue or project backlog.

For data-center power/cooling balance-of-plant, the highest-evidence chokepoint subnodes in this pass are medium-voltage switchgear, custom thermal-management equipment, liquid-cooling support systems, and field electrical/mechanical installation capacity.

Need a separate focused pass for US-listed installation/services names such as FIX and EME, transformer/grid-equipment suppliers, busway/copper component suppliers, and niche liquid-cooling component makers.
POWL should remain in the Layer 1B underfollowed lane for data-center electrical balance-of-plant because it has explicit data-center switchgear commentary and a greater-than-$400M data-center order.

MOD should remain in the Layer 1B underfollowed lane despite now exceeding the preferred $10B hunting range because its exposure is unusually direct after the Airedale data-center cooling LTA exceeding $4B.
ATKR is a weaker but useful second-order candidate; keep only if later evidence quantifies data-center revenue or backlog rather than generic electrical-products demand.

Future passes should test NVT, BE, AAON, FIX, EMCOR, and smaller pump/valve/heat-exchanger suppliers for liquid-cooling and installation-service exposure, but avoid overfilling the list with already repriced large-cap leaders.

POWL should be tracked as a mid-cap switchgear and packaged electrical-systems candidate for AI data-center balance-of-plant exposure; key survival test is recurring data-center backlog rather than one-off mega-projects.
AAON/BASX belongs in the cooling lane because management disclosed strong BASX data-center cooling demand, liquid/air-side cooling exposure, and record backlog.

BELFB is a lower-attention component-level hypothesis for data-center power conversion, protection, connectors, magnetics, and high-speed connectivity; evidence quality depends on segment-level AI/HPC revenue disclosure.

Need a later Layer 2 pass to separate true data-center power/cooling chokepoints from generic electrification exposure by verifying revenue mix, customer design-ins, lead times, capacity constraints, and margin inflection.
